question: What relative lengths are shown in Figure 6B-2 for a merging taper, shifting taper, and shoulder taper?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Figure 6B-2 dimensions the merging taper at a length of L, the shifting taper at ½ L, and the shoulder taper at ⅓ L. These relative lengths match the recommended taper lengths in Section 6B.08 and the criteria in Table 6B-3 ("at least L," "at least 0.5 L," and "at least 0.33 L," respectively), with L calculated using the formulas in Table 6B-4. Guidance (recommended): - "The appropriate taper length (L) should be determined using the criteria shown in Tables 6B-3 and 6B-4." - "A shifting taper should have a length of approximately ½ L (see Tables 6B-3 and 6B-4)." - "If used, shoulder tapers should have a length of approximately ¹⁄3 L (see Tables 6B-3 and 6B-4). If a shoulder is used as a travel lane, either through practice or during a TTC activity, a normal merging or shifting taper should be used." Options (permitted): - The lateral buffer space may be used to separate the traffic space from the work space, as shown in Figures 6B-1 and 6B-2; the figure also notes "*S = speed in mph" and "See Table 6B-4 for formulas for calculating taper length (L)." Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 6B-2 labels the merging taper with dimension "L," both shifting tapers with "1/2 L," and the shoulder taper with "1/3 L" (a "4S ft*" dimension is also shown for the tangent section between shifting tapers, where S = speed in mph). - [Image 2] Table 6B-3 lists taper length criteria: Merging Taper "at least L," Shifting Taper "at least 0.5 L," Shoulder Taper "at least 0.33 L," and 50–100 ft for one-lane, two-way and downstream tapers. - [Image 3] The full-page view of Figure 6B-2 (p.774) confirms the same relative dimensions: L for the merging taper, ½ L for the shifting tapers, and ⅓ L for the shoulder taper. - [Image 4] Page 776 shows the Section 6B.08 Guidance text recommending shifting tapers of approximately ½ L and shoulder tapers of approximately ⅓ L. - [Image 5] Figure 6B-3 (p.777) illustrates a related taper type—the one-lane, two-way traffic taper of 50 to 100 ft—not one of the three tapers dimensioned by L in Figure 6B-2. - [Image 6] Figure 6P-38 (p.935) shows an application using a shoulder taper and a shifting taper dimensioned at ½ L, consistent with Figure 6B-2. Citations: - Figure 6B-2 (p.774) - Table 6B-3 (p.775) - Section 6B.08 Support §2 (p.775) - Section 6B.08 Guidance §4 (p.775) - Section 6B.08 Guidance §8 (p.776) - Section 6B.08 Guidance §10 (p.776) - Section 6B.06 Option §14 (p.775)
gold_answer: Merging taper: L; shifting taper: 1/2 L; shoulder taper: 1/3 L.
